extractions.value: Patient had breast cancer (infiltrating duct carcinoma) with axillary lymphadenopathy; small fibre sensory neuropathy on skin biopsy; apparent encephalopathy; dysautonomia during spasms; neuropathology showed mild reactive gliosis in anterior horns of lumbar cord and mild diffuse reactive astrocytosis in frontal cortex, pons, and medulla; cause of death aspiration pneumonia.
extractions.quote: Fine needle aspiration of a soft tissue right axillary mass showed metastatic adenocarcinoma. On an open surgical procedure, inﬁltrating duct carcinoma of the breast was identiﬁed. Skin biopsy at three sites on the patient’s leg showed diminished epidermal nerve ﬁbre density and terminal axonal swelling distally, consistent with a small ﬁbre sensory neuropathy. Microscopically, the lumbar cord had mild reactive gliosis in the anterior horns but no evidence of inﬂammation. Sections of the frontal cortex, pons, and medulla showed mild diVuse reactive astrocytosis.
